source_text:
6.2,3 Κύριε, μὴ τῷ θυμῷ σου
ἐλέγξῃς με, μηδὲ τῇ ὀργῇ σου παιδεύσῃς με· ἐλέη σόν με, Κύριε· ο τι ἀσθενής εἰμι,
ι ασαί με, ο τι ἐταράχθη τὰ ὀστᾶ μου. Θυμός ἐστιν ὁρμὴ ἐπιθυμίας ἡμέρου ψυ χῆς,
κατ' ἐξοχὴν ἀμύνης. Λέγει ου ν· εἰ καὶ ἐξώτερος ὁ θυμὸς ἐλέγχει, καὶ ἡ ὁργὴ τά χιον
παιδεύει, ἐγώ γε διὰ τὴν ἀσθένειάν μου δεόμαι τοῦ ἐλέους σου, καὶ δι' α λλης ἐλεγ
χθῆναι καὶ παιδευθῆναι θεραπείας, οὐ τηλικούτους προσαγού σης πόνους. Θέλει γὰρ
καὶ μὴ θυμῷ Θεοῦ ἐλεγχθῆναι, καὶ μὴ παιδευθῆναι ἐν ὀργῇ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐλεηθῆναι,
ἀσθενὴς ω ν, καὶ ἰα θῆναι ἀπὸ τῆς ταραχῆς τῶν ὀστέων καὶ τῆς ψυχῆς αὐτοῦ. –
Σύμμαχος· ἐν χόλῳ, ἐν ἀνυπερθεσίᾳ.
pass_a_gloss: Lord, not with-the wrath of-you convict me, nor with-the anger of-you discipline me; have-mercy-on me, Lord; because weak I-am, heal me, because were-troubled the bones of-me. Wrath is impulse of-desire of-tame soul, according-to excellence of-defense. He-says then: if even more-outer the wrath convicts, and the anger more-quickly disciplines, I at-least through the weakness of-me I-need the mercy of-you, and through other to-be-convicted and to-be-disciplined healing, not such-great bringing-on labors. For he-wants both not with-wrath of-God to-be-convicted, and not to-be-disciplined in anger of-him, and to-be-mercied, weak being, and to-be-healed from the trouble of-the bones and of-the soul of-him. Symmachus: in gall, in unpostponement.
pass_b_english: “Lord, do not convict me with your wrath, nor discipline me with your anger; have mercy on me, Lord, because I am weak; heal me, because my bones were troubled” (Psalm 6:2-3).

Wrath is an impulse of desire of a tame soul, pre-eminently of defense. He says then: even if the more outward wrath convicts, and the anger more quickly disciplines, I at least, because of my weakness, need your mercy, and to be convicted and disciplined by another healing, which does not bring on such great labors.

For he wants both not to be convicted by the wrath of God, and not to be disciplined in his anger, and to be shown mercy, being weak, and to be healed from the trouble of his bones and of his soul. — Symmachus: in gall, in unpostponement.

choices.why: ἥμερος = tame/gentle, the philosophical definition of θυμός. Not ἡμέρα ‘day’.
rejected: of the day of the soul

choices.why: Comparative of ταχύ. OCR τά χιον is not χιών ‘snow’.
The translator, as elsewhere in this catena. Not ‘companion’ (σύμμαχος common noun).
Symmachus: without delay. Not ὑπέρθεσις as pride/overconfidence.
ἐλέγχω exposes; παιδεύω trains. Keep them distinct; neither is simply ‘punish’.
He asks to be convicted and disciplined by a treatment that does not bring on such great labors. Not ‘with treatment, not such burdens of yours’.

anf_compare.notes: ANF lacks this Greek catena as reading English.
